$schema: Shap3D.ai language file – fill in "code", "name" and every empty text; lines ending in "#en" are only hints with the English text and may stay or go.

errors.badCode#en: “{code}” is not a valid language code – e.g. “fr”, “es” or “pt-BR”.
errors.badJson#en: The file is not valid JSON: {error}
errors.sourceLanguage#en: English is the source language and cannot be imported.
errors.noMessages#en: The file has no “messages” with the texts.

plugin.description#en: German, French, Spanish, Arabic and more languages for the interface: language switch at the top next to light/dark, translation editor with areas, search, progress, live preview and “where is this text?”, import and export of language files (JSON) and a template for new languages.

editor.importTitle#en: Load a language file (JSON) – English takes it as changes, any other language is created or replaced
editor.exportTitle#en: Download the target language as a JSON file
editor.templateTitle#en: Download template.json: all texts empty, the English text as a hint
editor.newHint#en: The new language starts empty – the app shows missing texts in English. It is kept in this browser; “Export” turns it into a file.
editor.previewTitle#en: The app shows the target language while the editor is open – every change is visible right away
editor.placeholdersTitle#en: The translation must contain the same placeholders as the English text
editor.whereTitle#en: Where is this text? – briefly highlights it in the interface
editor.whereNone#en: The text is not visible right now – first open the menu, panel or tool it belongs to.
editor.storedHint#en: Changes are kept in this browser.
editor.confirmDelete#en: Delete the language “{name}” with all its translations?

i18n.templateHint#en: Shap3D.ai language file: fill in “code” (e.g. "fr"), “name” (e.g. "Français") and “dir” ("ltr" or "rtl") and every empty text. Lines with “#en” are only hints with the English text and may stay. Keep placeholders like {count} unchanged.

commands.toggleGridLabels#en: Labels on the axes and grid
commands.togglePurgeReminder#en: Remind to purge unused when saving

import.converterUnreachable#en: The local converter cannot be reached – start the app with “npm run dev” or “npm run preview”.
import.needsLocalServer#en: .skp and .blend files only work with the local server (“npm run dev” or “npm run preview”).
import.unsupported#en: The format .{ext} is not supported – more formats (FBX, Collada, 3DS, Blender …) come with the plugin “Import formats” (Plugins › Manage plugins).
import.maxFile#en: 3ds Max files (.max) can only be read by 3ds Max itself – save them there via File › Export as FBX (or .3ds/.obj) and import that file.
import.skipped#en: {count} triangle over the limit skipped | {count} triangles over the limit skipped

toast.cleared#en: Workspace cleared – Ctrl+Z brings everything back

confirm.resizeGroup#en: Do you want to resize the group's contents? (factor {factor})
confirm.resizeModel#en: Do you want to resize the model? (factor {factor})
confirm.purgeOnSave#en: {count} unused group or component – purge it before saving? | {count} unused groups or components – purge them before saving?

status.place#en: Place “{name}”: click the target position. Arrow keys rotate by 90°.
status.select#en: Click or drag to select objects. Shift = add/remove. Ctrl = add. Shift + Ctrl = remove.
status.lasso#en: Draw a loop around objects. Clockwise = fully inside, counter-clockwise = touching.
status.eraser#en: Click or drag over edges to delete them. Shift = hide, Ctrl = soften.
status.paint#en: Material “{material}”: click to paint faces. Alt = sample material, Ctrl = connected faces, Shift = all matching faces.
status.sample#en: Click a face to pick up its material.
status.lineEnd#en: Click to set the end point, or type a length. | Arrow keys = lock inference direction on/off. Shift = lock inference.
status.lineStart#en: Click to set the first end point. | Arrow keys = lock inference direction on/off.
status.freehand#en: Click and drag to draw a freehand curve.
status.rectangleCorner#en: Click to set the opposite corner, or type length and width (e.g. 2000; 1500).
status.rectangleStart#en: Click to set the first corner.
status.rotrect2#en: Pick the second corner (length and direction).
status.rotrect3#en: Pick the width and the angle.
status.circleRadius#en: Pick or type the radius. ({count} segments; “12s” changes the number)
status.polygonRadius#en: Pick or type the radius. ({count} sides; “12s” changes the number)
status.circleCenter#en: Pick the centre. Type e.g. “48s” to change the segments.
status.polygonCenter#en: Pick the centre. Type e.g. “8s” to change the sides.
status.arc2Start#en: Pick the start point of the arc.
status.arc3Second#en: Pick a second point on the arc.
status.pushpullDistance#en: Click to set the distance, or type it. | Snaps to corners, edges and faces. {mode}
status.pushpullPick#en: Click the face to push or pull. | Double-click = repeat the last distance. {mode}
status.offsetDistance#en: Move the cursor to set the offset, or type a distance.
status.moveTarget#en: Click to set the target point, or type a distance. | Ctrl = copy on/off. Arrow keys = lock inference direction.
status.moveTargetCopy#en: Click to set the target point, or type a distance. (copy) | Ctrl = copy on/off. Arrow keys = lock inference direction.
status.moveStart#en: Click to set the start point. | Ctrl = copy on/off.
status.rotateCenter#en: Pick the centre of rotation. Arrow keys align the protractor.
status.rotateStart#en: Pick the start point of the rotation angle.
status.rotateAngle#en: Pick or type the rotation angle. Ctrl = copy.
status.scaleDrag#en: Drag to scale, or type a factor. Ctrl = about the centre, Shift = uniform.
status.followmeProfile#en: Click the profile face that should follow the selected path.
status.followmePath#en: First select edges as the path (e.g. double-clicking a face selects its edges), then this tool.
status.tapeEnd#en: Pick the end point. Ctrl switches: measure › guide line › guide point.
status.tapeStart#en: Pick the start point (point or edge).
status.tapeStartGuides#en: Pick the start point (point or edge). Guides are created.
status.tapeStartPoint#en: Pick the start point (point or edge). A guide point is created at the end point.
status.dimensionStart#en: Pick the start point of the dimension or an edge.
status.dimensionPlace#en: Drag the dimension to its position.
status.textPlace#en: Pick the position of the text.
status.textAnchor#en: Pick the point the text should point to.
status.section#en: Click a face to place a section plane. Arrow keys align it with the axes.
status.orbit#en: Drag to rotate the view. Shift = pan.
status.zoom#en: Drag up/down to zoom. Shift = change field of view. Type a field-of-view angle (e.g. 35°).
status.zoomwindow#en: Drag a rectangle to zoom into that area.
status.lookaround#en: Drag to look around (the camera turns on the spot).
status.walk#en: Drag up/down to walk, left/right to turn. Arrow keys work too.
status.poscam#en: Click to place the camera there at eye height.

errors.assetMissing#en: File “{path}” is missing in the plugin package
errors.importerNeedsHandler#en: An importer needs import or loadScene
errors.importerExists#en: There already is a plugin import for .{ext}
errors.noExport#en: The module exports no plugin (export default { … })
errors.badId#en: Plugin id missing or invalid (only a–z, 0–9 and -)
errors.builtinReplace#en: “{id}” is a built-in plugin and cannot be replaced
errors.mainMissing#en: The main file “{path}” from package.json is missing in the folder

app.dropToImport#en: Drop the file to import it

theme.hintDarkMenus#en: Only the menus are dark, the 3D scene stays light.
theme.hintNightScene#en: Light menus, the 3D scene shows night.
theme.hintAllDark#en: All dark: menus and the 3D scene at night.

palette.keepOpenTitle#en: Run or toggle, the palette stays open
palette.placeholder#en: Search everything: tools, commands, panels, switches, materials …

toolbar.searchTitle#en: Command palette – search everything (Ctrl+Shift+P, F1 or Shift twice)

materials.hint#en: Click a material, then faces (paint bucket, B).

tags.assignTitle#en: Assign the selection to the highlighted tag
tags.hint#en: Double-click renames. Hidden tags hide every entity with that tag.
tags.toScenesTitle#en: Apply the visibility of the highlighted tag to scenes
tags.toScenesVisible#en: “{tag}” is visible – show it in these scenes:
tags.toScenesHidden#en: “{tag}” is hidden – hide it in these scenes:
tags.appliedToScenes#en: “{tag}” applied to {count} scene | “{tag}” applied to {count} scenes

scenes.empty#en: No scenes yet. Scenes store camera, style and visible tags.

components.empty#en: No components. Select geometry and press “G”.
components.libraryHint#en: Library objects are built by a script and then placed at the cursor.

soften.hint#en: Softens edges between faces of the selection whose angle is smaller than the value set.

shadows.hint#en: The sun position is calculated for about 48° north. Even without shadows it sets the lighting of the faces.

outliner.empty#en: No groups or components in the model.

display.empty#en: No section planes. Tool “Section plane” in the expanded tool set.
display.rulers#en: Rulers on the axes (m · cm · mm depending on zoom)
display.grid#en: Ground grid (mm · cm · m depending on zoom)
display.labels#en: Labels along the axes and grid legend (5 m · Grid 1 m · 10 m)

select.desc#en: Selects entities for other tools and commands.
select.step2#en: Drag from left to right (window) or right to left (crossing).
select.step3#en: Double-click: face with edges or open a group. Triple-click: everything connected.

line.desc#en: Draws edges. Closed edges in one plane form a face automatically.
line.step2#en: Click the end point or type a length.
line.step3#en: Keep drawing or press Esc to finish.

rectangle.desc#en: Draws rectangular faces on the ground or on existing faces.
rectangle.step3#en: Type e.g. “3m;4m” to set the size (also afterwards).

circle.desc#en: Draws a circle (a polygon with many segments).
circle.step1#en: Optional: type the number of segments (e.g. “48”).
circle.step3#en: Click for the radius or type it.

arc2.desc#en: Draws an arc through two end points and a bulge.
arc2.step3#en: Drag the bulge and click (a half circle snaps).

arc.desc#en: Draws an arc from centre, start point and angle.
arc.step3#en: Click or type the end angle.

arc3.desc#en: Draws an arc through three points.
arc3.step2#en: Click a point on the arc.

pie.desc#en: Draws a circle sector as a face.

freehand.step1#en: Press the mouse button and drag.
freehand.step2#en: Releasing ends the curve; close to the start it closes.

pushpull.desc#en: Extrudes faces into 3D solids or moves them.
pushpull.step2#en: Move the mouse and click again or type a distance.
pushpull.step3#en: Double-clicking another face repeats the last distance.

offset.desc#en: Creates a parallel copy of the face's edges inwards or outwards.
offset.step2#en: Move the cursor and click or type the distance.

move.step1#en: Select entities (or point right at them).
move.step3#en: Click the target point or type a distance.

rotate.step2#en: Click the centre of rotation (the protractor aligns with faces).
rotate.step3#en: Click the start angle, then click or type the rotation angle.
rotate.mod2#en: Arrow keys: align the protractor with an axis

scale.step3#en: Drag or type a factor (e.g. “2” or “1;2;1”, also a length “3m”).

tape.step1#en: Click the start point (or an edge for a parallel guide).
tape.step2#en: Click the end point – the length is in the “Measurements” box.
tape.step3#en: Type a new length to scale the model.
tape.step4#en: Double-click: a single guide point right there.
tape.mod1#en: Ctrl: measure only › guide lines › guide point

protractor.desc#en: Measures angles and creates angled guides.

dimension.step1#en: Click the start and end point (or an edge).
dimension.step2#en: Drag the dimension to its position and click.

text.desc#en: Creates labels with a leader line.
text.step1#en: Click an entity (a face shows its area, an edge its length).

section.desc#en: Cuts the model to show the inside.
section.step1#en: Point at a face (the plane aligns with it).
section.step3#en: Switch it on/off in the “Display” panel.

eraser.desc#en: Deletes edges (and the faces next to them).
eraser.step1#en: Click edges or drag over them.

paint.desc#en: Assigns materials to faces, groups and components.
paint.step1#en: Pick a material in the “Materials” panel.
paint.mod3#en: Shift: all matching faces in the model

orbit.desc#en: Rotates the camera around the model.
orbit.step2#en: The middle mouse button works in every tool.

pan.step2#en: Shift + middle mouse button in every tool.

zoom.step2#en: The mouse wheel zooms towards the cursor.

followme.desc#en: Extrudes a profile along a path (e.g. pipe, cornice, lathe shape).
followme.step1#en: Select the path edges (double-clicking a face selects its edges).

mesh.noTopFaces#en: The object has no faces on its top level.
mesh.tooMany#en: Too many polygons ({count} triangles) – that would slow the browser down.
mesh.cannotSimplify#en: The object cannot be simplified that much.
mesh.moreKeepTitle#en: Every triangle becomes four – the shape stays exactly the same
mesh.moreRoundTitle#en: Every triangle becomes four, corners and curves get smoother
mesh.affectsComponent#en: Works on the top level of the group/component – and so on all its copies. Undo with Ctrl+Z.
mesh.affectsGroup#en: Works on the top level of the group/component. Undo with Ctrl+Z.
mesh.selectHint#en: Select a group, component or drawn circle to change its polygon count. Combine loose geometry with “Make group” first.
mesh.exactHint#en: The object is rebuilt exactly with the new resolution.
mesh.circleHint#en: Works while the circle is still flat – set it before Push/Pull.
mesh.noMesh#en: No mesh found – expected lines like “v 1 2 3” and “f 1 2 3”.
mesh.fewAlready#en: The object already has very few polygons.

welcome.text#en: Easy 3D modelling right in the browser – with an AI that runs on your own computer. A few short steps show you the essentials.

draw.text#en: Draw a face on the ground and pull it up with Push/Pull – that is how walls, furniture and whole houses are made.

navigate.text#en: With the mouse you move freely through your model.
navigate.tip1#en: Drag the middle mouse button = rotate (orbit)

ai.text#en: Just describe what you want – “a table with 4 chairs” or “a spider with red eyes” – and the AI builds it. It runs locally, e.g. with Ollama; a wizard helps with the setup.

more.text#en: Shape mountains and valleys with the terrain tool, build objects by script (s3d.box …) or simply drag files from SketchUp, Blender, 3ds Max & co. into the window.
more.tip1#en: Tool Terrain – brushes for hills, valleys and textures
more.tip2#en: Script editor on the right – with API info and examples
more.tip3#en: SKP · BLEND · FBX · 3DS · DAE · OBJ · STL · glTF …

look.text#en: At the top you switch between light and dark – also just the menus or a night scene. You will find this introduction in the menu at any time.
look.tip1#en: ☾ / ☀ top left – the arrow next to it has more options

box.desc#en: Box from the front left bottom corner. Width = X, depth = Y, height = Z.

cylinder.desc#en: Upright cylinder standing on its centre. segments = number of sides (default 24).

cylinderBetween.desc#en: Cylinder or cone between any two points – ideal for legs, branches, pipes, railings. endRadius = radius at the end (0 = point).

cone.desc#en: Cone with its tip at the top. With endRadius > 0 a truncated cone (lampshade, bucket, flower pot).

pyramid.desc#en: Pyramid with a square (sides 4) or n-sided base. kante = length of a base edge.

prism.desc#en: Upright prism with a regular n-sided base (default 6 = hexagon).

sphere.desc#en: Sphere around a centre with smoothed edges.

dome.desc#en: Half sphere with a flat bottom – domes, lamps, igloos.

ellipsoid.desc#en: Stretched sphere with three radii – bodies, heads, cushions, leaves, stones.

tube.desc#en: Hollow cylinder – pipes, cups, rings, wells.

torus.desc#en: Lying ring – tyres, life buoys, donuts, handles.

wedge.desc#en: Ramp rising along +X to its height – ramps, lean-to roofs, wedges.

stairs.desc#en: Straight stairs along +X. Default: 10 steps, 17.5 cm high, 28 cm deep, 1 m wide.

mesh.desc#en: Triangle mesh from “v x y z” and “f a b c” lines (e.g. LLaMA-Mesh). size = longest side.

rect.desc#en: Rectangular face. ebene 'xy' = lying, 'xz' / 'yz' = standing. Then e.g. .pushpull(höhe).

circle.desc#en: Circular face. normal = direction the face points to ('z', 'x', 'y' or a vector).

face.desc#en: Any flat face from at least 3 points that lie in one plane.

polyhedron.desc#en: Exact geometry like OpenSCAD's polyhedron: punkte = [[x,y,z], …], flächen = lists of point numbers (from 0), e.g. [0, 1, 2, 3], or { outer: [...], holes: [[...]], material: 'Holz' } for faces with holes. This is also the code “Open as code” produces.

line.desc#en: Edges without thickness. A closed flat polyline forms a face automatically.

arc.desc#en: Circular arc as edges. Returns the points – handy as a path for followMe.

pushpull.desc#en: Pulls a face into a solid. For lying faces a positive value always goes up.

extrude.desc#en: Like pushpull, but in a fixed direction: 'x', 'y', 'z', '-x', '-y', '-z' or a vector.

offset.desc#en: Draws an inner outline into the face – for frames, windows, borders.

followMe.desc#en: Sweeps a profile along a path – pipes, cornices, frames, lathe shapes.

faceMaterial.desc#en: Set the material of the front or back of a single face; reverse() flips the face.

group.desc#en: Everything created in the callback is combined into one group.

component.desc#en: Reusable definition – build it once, place it as often as you like. Changes affect all copies.

transform.desc#en: All solid functions return a group that can be changed like this (chainable).

copy.desc#en: Copy with offset; material for the whole group; assign a tag; hide; explode into loose geometry.

useMaterial.desc#en: All materials in the list below work directly by their name – without creating them first.

material.desc#en: Defines a material or changes an existing one. texture = one of the textures below, size = tile size in metres.

materials.desc#en: Names of the ready-made materials (optionally only one category, e.g. 'Metall') or of the textures.

view.desc#en: Pick a standard view and zoom to everything (done after the script).

camera.desc#en: Put the camera at a position and point it at a target.

shadows.desc#en: Shadows on/off with time of day; change the display – faceStyle: 'textured' | 'shaded' | 'monochrome' | 'hiddenline' | 'wireframe', xray: true = X-ray.

annot.desc#en: Dimension line between two points, label with arrow, guide line or guide point.

tag.desc#en: Create tags (layers), show/hide them and assign groups.

clear.desc#en: Empties the model (or the current group). Like everything in a script it can be undone with Ctrl+Z.

units.desc#en: All numbers are metres. Wherever a length is expected, strings with a unit work too.

points.desc#en: Points are arrays. The ground is at z = 0.

random.desc#en: Plain JavaScript – loops, variables and maths are allowed.

log.desc#en: Writes to the console below the editor. s3d.stats() returns the number of faces/edges.

apiReference.insertTitle#en: Insert the example at the cursor
apiReference.tryTitle#en: Build the example into the model right away (one undo step)
apiReference.tryMaterial#en: Build a cube with this material

completion.ownSuggestions#en: The editor has its own suggestions for “{language}”

api.point#en: Point [x, y, z] – the same as an array.
api.length#en: Convert a length with a unit to metres.
api.warn#en: Write a warning to the console.
api.textures#en: Names of the textures for s3d.material(…, { texture }).
api.polyline#en: Polyline; closed and flat it becomes a face.
api.zoomExtents#en: Zoom to everything after the script.

group.moveTo#en: Put the origin at a point.
group.rotate#en: Rotate about an axis ('x', 'y', 'z' or a vector), by default about the group's origin.
group.tag#en: Assign a tag (layer) – created when needed.
group.copy#en: Copy with offset – returns the copy.
group.explode#en: Explode into loose geometry. Returns the number of parts.
group.name#en: Name of the group or component.
group.ref#en: Reference { kind, id } to the instance.

face.pushpull#en: Pull into a solid. For lying faces positive always goes up.
face.extrude#en: Like pushpull, but in a fixed direction: 'x', 'y', 'z', '-x', '-y', '-z' or a vector.
face.offset#en: Draw an inner outline into the face.
face.followMe#en: Sweep a profile along a path.
face.ref#en: Reference { kind, id } to the face.

component.place#en: Place a copy of the component.

completion.console#en: Writes to the console below the editor.

options.material#en: Material name – ready-made materials work directly by their name.
options.group#en: false = loose geometry instead of a group.
options.sides#en: Number of sides of the base.
options.normal#en: Direction the face points to ('x', 'y', 'z' or a vector).
options.smooth#en: Edges flatter than this angle (degrees) are smoothed.
options.children#en: List of the objects in the group.
options.faces#en: Faces as lists of point numbers (from 0).

completion.units#en: Wherever a length is expected, strings with a unit work.
completion.s3d#en: The Shap3D.ai script API – solids, faces, groups, materials, view.
completion.consoleObject#en: console.log(…) writes to the console below the editor.

pluginManager.loadFolderTitle#en: Folder with package.json – e.g. the built dist folder of a plugin package
pluginManager.updateAllTitle#en: Read every package installed from a folder again – e.g. after npm run build
pluginManager.warning#en: Plugins are JavaScript modules and run with full access to the application. Only install plugins whose source you trust. They are stored in this browser only.
pluginManager.updateTitle#en: Read the package from its folder again – e.g. after npm run build
pluginManager.howTo#en: How to write your own plugins is described in the README under “Plugins”. The examples are in
pluginManager.loadFailed#en: The plugin could not be loaded: {error}

scriptEditor.convertTitle#en: Translate the code into another format – the model stays unchanged
scriptEditor.undoConvertTitle#en: Bring back the code from before the conversion
scriptEditor.newTitle#en: Empty script in the chosen language – Ctrl+Z brings the previous code back
scriptEditor.yUpTitle#en: OBJ files and LLaMA-Mesh are Y-up – turned to Z-up
scriptEditor.smoothTitle#en: Edges between faces flatter than this angle are smoothed (0 = all edges visible)
scriptEditor.consoleHint#en: Output of s3d.log(…) and errors appear here. Every run is a single undo step.
scriptEditor.objHelp#en:
OBJ mesh: lines “v x y z” (vertex) and “f a b c …” (face, vertex numbers from 1).
Everything else (text, # comments, vn/vt, groups) is ignored – raw LLaMA-Mesh output
can be pasted directly. The mesh is scaled to “Size” (longest side),
put on the ground and placed as a component next to the model.
In a JS script: s3d.mesh(objText, { at: [x, y, z], size: '80cm', yUp: true, material: 'Holz' })
scriptEditor.converted#en: Converted to {format} – the model is unchanged. “Run” builds it in.
scriptEditor.placeholder#en:
New script, e.g.
{start}

Ctrl+Space shows suggestions, “Load example…” ready-made scripts.
Run with Ctrl+Enter.
scriptEditor.newHint#en: New script – Ctrl+Z in the editor brings the previous code back.
scriptEditor.objDetected#en: OBJ mesh detected – language set to “OBJ mesh”
scriptEditor.done#en: Done – {count} face in the model. | Done – {count} faces in the model.

house.description#en: Box + roof prism, door and windows as groups.

stairs.description#en: Steps with a for loop, sizes as variables.

spiral.description#en: Define a component once, then place it rotated.

fence.description#en: Posts & slats as components – changes affect all copies.

city.description#en: Grid of high-rises with random height and colour.

lathe.description#en: Turn a profile along a circle – like “Follow me”.

json-shelf.description#en: “array” repeats an object with an offset.

mesh-js.description#en: Embed OBJ text right in the script, scale it and place it several times.

obj-chair.description#en: Raw LLaMA-Mesh output – only v/f lines. Set size and axes above.

errors.faceFailed#en: The face could not be created (points not in one plane?)
errors.tubeRadius#en: tube: the inner radius must be between 0 and the outer radius
errors.async#en: Asynchronous scripts are not supported – “await” is ignored.
errors.needsText3d#en: 3D text needs the plugin “3D text” (plugin manager)

codeExport.header#en: Made with Shap3D.ai from {source} – sizes in metres
codeExport.objSize#en: Size: {size} m (longest side) – enter it as “Size” in the script editor
codeExport.failed#en: The code could not be run
codeExport.nothing#en: No faces or edges to convert

splash.webglTitle#en: 3D graphics (WebGL) are switched off in the browser right now
splash.webglText#en: {name} needs WebGL to draw the 3D view. The browser reports that it cannot create a WebGL context – usually because the graphics card was blocked for this session after a driver crash.
splash.webglRestart#en: Close the browser completely and start it again
splash.webglRestartHint#en: (all windows) – that almost always solves it.
splash.webglStatus#en: Check the status at {chrome} or {edge} – it should say “WebGL: Hardware accelerated”.
splash.webglDrivers#en: Update the graphics driver; with many open 3D tabs close some of them.
splash.failedText#en: An error occurred while starting. Details are in the browser console (F12).
